drivingQuestion: Does the incense precede the preparation of the lamps or follow it?
outcomeNote: The contradiction is posed; its resolution lies beyond this unit.

segments.he: וּמַקְטִיר אֶת הַקְּטוֹרֶת וּמֵטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת. אַלְמָא קְטוֹרֶת בְּרֵישָׁא וַהֲדַר נֵרוֹת. וּרְמִינְהוּ: מִי שֶׁזָּכָה בְּדִישּׁוּן מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי, וּמִי שֶׁזָּכָה בַּמְּנוֹרָה, וּמִי שֶׁזָּכָה בַּקְּטוֹרֶת!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that on each of the seven days the High Priest «burns the incense and removes» the ashes from «the lamps. Apparently, incense» is burned «first, and then the lamps» are cleaned. «And» the Gemara «raises a contradiction» from a mishna in tractate Tamid that discusses the lottery in which the priests performing the various tasks that constitute the morning Temple service are selected. That mishna first mentions the one «who was privileged» to be selected to perform «removal of the ashes from the inner altar,» and then «the one who was privileged» to be selected to remove the ashes from the lamps of «the candelabrum,» and only then does it deal with «the one who is privileged» to be selected to burn «the incense.» According to that mishna, removing ashes from the candelabrum precedes the burning of the incense.
